answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut mandate is severe and non-negotiable. Switching vendors (memory_c2) worked before but risks integration disruption given 94% line utilization with no buffer. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable—the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renewal, leaving us unprotected. Renewing at current terms (memory_c1) foregoes the cost recovery opportunity. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses risk but doesn't directly meet the 18% cost target. Renegotiating the incumbent (memory_c4) previously recovered real margin through benchmarking; with an expiring contract and explicit cost pressure, we have maximum leverage now. I am verifying memory_c4 to confirm the negotiation mechanics and magnitude of prior recovery. A standard negotiation experiment (not broad rollout, not minimal test) allows us to push aggressively on both price and terms while preserving the incumbent relationship and delivery stability. This approach directly targets the cost mandate, respects the 14-day deadline, and keeps the line running. Downstream risk is flagged because hitting 18% cuts while maintaining 94% utilization leaves no margin for error; uncertainty about vendor willingness to move enough is preserved rather than assumed away.
